newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian stocks ease off record run at close.
newsitem.headline: Australian stocks ease off record run at close.

text.p: SPI futures 2628 -13 US 30yr cl 6.84 +0.02
10yrbond futs 92.765 -0.030 Gold NY 343.95 Lon fix 343.75
*Stocks ease off record highs by close as investors book profits and buyers stay quiet. Volume 388.38 million, A$887.61 million, 1,213 stocks traded, 371 steady, 341 up, 501 down.
The Australian stock market eased off its record breaking run by Wednesday's close as investors booked profits.
Brokers said a large portfolio went through the market, boosting trade in a see-saw session.
At 4.25 p.m. (0625 GMT), the All Ordinaries index closed at 2,613.7 points, down 15.2 points from Tuesday's record close and off the fresh intra-day high of 2,635.7 hit earlier in the day.
Volume was active with over A$880 million worth of trade.
The June share price index futures closed 13 points lower, narrowing its premium to 14.3 points over the underlying index.
"The market has had a good run and there were a few people that wanted to lock a few profits in," said Gordon Furner, a trader at brokers ABN AMRO Hoare Govett in Sydney.

The market's largest sector, the bank index, was among the biggest to fall, with all four major banks down after Tuesday's strong jump, helped by the Reserve Bank of Australia's (RBA) loosening of prime asset ratio requirements.
"It (RBA announcement) was very neutral for earnings," said Furner. NAB and Commonwealth Bank were the biggest fallers among the banks both down 20 cents to A$18.77 and A$14.30 respectively.
Market heavyweight BHP joined the long list of blue-chip stocks falling, down 26 cents at A$18.66.

"BHP keeps struggling. When it failed to break through A$19 dollars, some investors started selling off," one Brisbane-based dealer said. Brokers said a big portfolio crossing by brokerage BZW Australia dominated trade.

Data released earlier in the day shook off doubts about a housing industry recovery in 1997 after a strong rise in April housing finance approvals, helped the building material index to a higher finisher. It was the only major sector to end the day in the positive zone.
Transport and healthcare group Mayne Nickless was another stock to tumble, down over two percent.
"There is a perception that the Optus float won't happen now until next year...It is a perception that is not helping Mayne," ABN's Furner said.
Mayne owns about 25 percent of telephone carrier Optus, which has said it plans a sharemarket float later this year.

In other market news, Australian bonds ended little changed, recovering from a weak opening after two gloomy surveys kept alive thoughts of a policy easing. At 5.05 p.m. (0705 GMT) the 10-year T-bond was at 7.23 percent, up two basis points.

The Australian dollar struck to familar grounds on its U.S. counterpart, but went on a whistle stop tour of yen levels not seen in 10 months. At 5.10 p.m. (0710 GMT), the dollar was at US$0.7601/06 compared with US$0.7610/15 late here on Tuesday. -------------------------(TECHNICALS)---------------------------
